editorial:
Imagine you are a teenager just trying to make some easy money by house-sitting a giant, empty mansion in London. That is where you meet Joe, a kid who finds himself in a weird situation when he meets Elliot, the rich and eccentric owner of the house. You will feel the strange energy between them right away. Elliot is not your typical boss; he is mysterious and a bit off, making you wonder what he is actually hiding behind his wealth. The movie feels like a slow burn that focuses more on the odd friendship and the secrets hiding in the walls than on a fast plot.

What really works here is the acting, as you can feel the tension grow every time these two are on screen together. Some parts might feel a bit slow if you are looking for big explosions, but the quiet moments make the surprises hit harder. If you enjoy character studies, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, or if you love having a physical library, adding the Blu-ray to your collection is a great move. It is a solid pick for a rainy Sunday afternoon.
endingExplained: The story wraps up when the truth about Elliot's past and his loneliness comes to light. You see that the house was more of a cage than a palace. Joe eventually realizes that money cannot fix the emptiness in Elliot's life. The movie ends with a bittersweet feeling as Joe moves on, having learned a tough lesson about adulthood and the hidden sadness that often comes with extreme wealth and isolation.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character dramas and mysterious friendships.
